question: What does it mean for vectors to span a space?
direct_answer: Their linear combinations can produce every vector in that space.
expanded_answer: The span of a set of vectors is the collection of all vectors you can make by taking linear combinations of them. If a set spans a space, then it is enough to represent any vector in that space. This is why basis vectors are so important: they are a compact generating set.
key_points: A spanning set can represent every vector in the space
common_wrong_ideas: Spanning means vectors are similar to each other
A spanning set must be minimal
Span is only about geometric area, not representability
